newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Puerto Rican telecom privatization possible.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rican telecom privatization possible.

text.p: Puerto Rico's legislature is lining up behind the proposed privatization of the government-owned Puerto Rico Telephone Co (PRTC) after opposing an earlier selloff attempt.
A transaction to a single buyer or one involving several taking pieces of PRTC, which has 1.135 million local lines, could be done by year's end, government officials said.
"The telephone company is losing market value every day, week and month that passes," Senate President Charlie Rodriguez told the San Juan Star newspaper.

Off-island phone companies which eyed the property in 1990, when privatizing PRTC was last proposed, and phone companies with big business links to Puerto Rico were the most likely buyers, consultants and government and industry sources said.

The government said on Monday it was putting PRTC on the block and intended to hire a consultant to sort through three main options: an outright sale of the entire company, a unit-by-unit sale, or a public share offering. "There's interest out there," the head of Puerto Rico's privatization program, Marcos Rodriguez Ema, told journalists late Monday.
Potential buyers of all or parts of PRTC include Stamford, Conn.-based GTE Corp, BellSouth Corp of Atlanta and Spain's Telefonica de Espana, government and industry sources here said.
All three companies expressed interest in PRTC in 1990, and Telefonica bought a majority stake in PRTC's long-distance unit five years ago for $142 million.

Consultant Andrew Fyfe of Price Waterhouse in Washington, D.C., said NYNEX Corp was another possible buyer because of the extensive telephone traffic between Puerto Rico and its important New York market.

Still another possible buyer, government and industry sources here said, was cellular group Centennial de Puerto Rico, which is already investing $500 million in the island's telecoms sector. It competes against PRTC's cellular unit.
The value of PRTC is unclear, although government officials and industry sources said Puerto Rico's government would likely have gotten a better price in the early 1990s.
An industry rule of thumb, which values telephone access lines between $2,000 and $3,000 each, would put PRTC's value at anywhere from $2.2 billion to $3.4 billion.

But PRTC's revenues dropped 16 percent to $107 million in 1996 from the previous year because it reduced intra-island rates as a pre-emptive strike against private firms gearing up to enter the $250 million market.
Consultant Fyfe said PRTC had room for good expansion, since the penetration of telephone lines at 30 per 100 residents was less than half the rate in the mainland U.S.
Seven years ago, when former Gov. Rafael Hernandez Colon tried to sell off PRTC, price was a key sticking point. The legislature imposed a rigid price structure which crippled the sale.
But some leaders of the pro-statehood New Progressive Party, which controls the Commonwealth Legislature, are supporting the privatization this time around, despite union opposition.
